evidence: start: How did we respond? - timeline puts the beginning of intermittent management-operation failures across networking services at 20:30 UTC on 30 Sep. end: How did we respond? - rollback finished in all affected regions at 02:15 UTC on 1 Oct, when customer impact stopped. regions: What happened? - a list of 33 named regions across several geographies is given as affected.
notes: no publication date shown; the unlabeled date 09/30/2026 at the top matches the incident start date and cannot be the publication date, since the report describes events of 1 October 2026. Region programmatic names derived from the 33 display names by Azure's naming convention (lowercase, no spaces); newer regions (e.g. India South Central, Belgium Central, Chile Central) were not checked against a source. region_starts empty: the report says impact times varied by region with a rolling update but gives no per-region times. services_n counts ExpressRoute Gateway, Application Gateway, Azure Firewall, Azure Bastion, Virtual WAN, VPN Gateway and Azure VMware Solution (the last as may have lost connectivity). ExpressRoute connectivity self-restored at 22:36 UTC; management impact continued to 02:15 UTC.

evidence: start: What happened? and How did we respond? - impact from unstable service instances began at 10:03 UTC on 29 Sep. end: How did we respond? - by 15:58 UTC availability was back and the impact was declared mitigated. regions: What happened? - the affected AI services were those hosted in the Sweden Central region.
notes: no publication date shown; the unlabeled date 09/29/2026 at the top matches the incident date. end_basis impact_ended because the report states service availability had recovered at 15:58 UTC. The internal deployment began 09:38 UTC and traffic surged at 10:00 UTC, before customer impact. No zone named. Services: Azure OpenAI Service, Foundry Agent Service, Foundry Models, Azure AI services.

evidence: start: How did we respond? - the break-fix work started at 14:44 UTC, given as the earliest possible customer impact. end: How did we respond? - at 19:41 UTC all services were back at expected levels and impact was declared mitigated. regions: What happened? - traffic entering or leaving the West US region was disrupted; traffic inside the region was unaffected.
notes: no publication date shown; the unlabeled date 07/23/2026 at the top matches the incident date. Start is stated as the earliest potential customer impact. Datacenter-to-WAN connectivity was restored at 18:26 UTC when the rollback completed; services fully recovered by 19:41 UTC, coded as end. No zone named. services_n counts the 23 listed services (incl. Microsoft Sentinel and Power BI Embedded); downstream Microsoft 365 impact, communicated separately (MO1437424), is not counted.

evidence: start: How did we respond? - first wave of retry amplification tied to the Australia East rollout began customer impact at 09:20 UTC. end: How did we respond? - after isolation, rollback and backlog clearing, impact was declared mitigated at 17:05 UTC. regions: What happened? and What went wrong - Australia East and Sweden Central named; impact strongest in European regions and Australia East.
notes: no publication date shown; the unlabeled date 05/29/2026 at the top matches the incident date. Conflict: the summary gives 09:39 to 17:05 UTC, but the timeline says customer impact began at 09:20 UTC (09:39 is when monitoring detected it); the timeline's 09:20 is coded. Impact spread across multiple regions; only Australia East and Sweden Central are named, other European regions are not named. region_starts: first wave in Australia East at 09:20 UTC; the issue reoccurred in Sweden Central at 14:40 UTC after the rollout reached it (Sweden Central may also have been in the unnamed first-wave regions). The 17:05 UTC end includes clearing of backlogged requests; no earlier impact-end time is given. Timeline lists 16:25 after 16:30 as printed. Only Azure OpenAI Service is named as impaired; Microsoft 365 was the upstream source.

evidence: start: How did we respond? - customer impact started at 04:24 UTC on 29 May as thermal alerts fired. end: How did we respond? - by 20:18 UTC every affected service was recovered except two telemetry services still working through backlogs. regions: What happened? - West US 2, with infrastructure shut down in two physical availability zones, AZ-01 and AZ-03.
notes: no publication date shown; the unlabeled date 05/29/2026 at the top matches the incident date. Zones are physical AZ labels as the report gives them (AZ-01, AZ-03), not logical zone numbers; Azure has no other zone code here. End coded at 20:18 UTC: Application Insights and Log Analytics then only processed accumulated backlogs until 02:30 UTC on 30 May (the summary's end), which rule 7 excludes. Power sags began 04:14 UTC, before customer impact. About 95% of impacted VMs had recovered by 12:00 UTC. services_n counts the 23 services listed as among those affected.

evidence: start: How did we respond? - failures and delays in provisioning, scaling or updating resources started at 11:30 UTC on 24 Apr. end: How did we respond? - at 23:22 UTC all customer impact was declared mitigated. regions: What happened? - East US, starting in physical AZ-01 and later spreading to AZ-02 and AZ-03.
notes: no publication date shown; the unlabeled date 04/24/2026 at the top matches the incident date. Zones are physical AZ labels as given (logical zones may map differently). Zone starts differ but rule 9 covers regions only: AZ-01 at 11:30 UTC (detected 11:38), AZ-03 at 13:50 UTC, AZ-02 at 19:05 UTC. Two timeline entries (13:14, 17:19) carry no UTC label. services_n counts the 18 listed services; the report adds that more dependent services may have been affected.

evidence: start: How did we respond? - customers began seeing unavailability and delayed monitoring data at 07:58 UTC on 7 Feb after UPS batteries ran out. end: How did we respond? - all affected services were declared mitigated at 04:24 UTC on 8 Feb. regions: What happened? - a power loss in one datacenter disrupted services in the West US region.
notes: no publication date shown; the unlabeled date 02/07/2026 at the top matches the incident date. One datacenter in West US; the report says West US has no Availability Zones, so no zone. Interim points: storage recovery complete 19:05 UTC, compute long tail mitigated 23:30 UTC on 7 Feb; Application Insights delayed telemetry ran to 04:24 UTC on 8 Feb. The report does not describe the last hours as backlog processing, so 04:24 UTC is kept. Return to utility power on 9 Feb is not customer impact. services_n: 24 listed entries, with Confidential VM types counted under Azure Virtual Machines (Application Insights counted separately from Azure Monitor as listed).

evidence: start: How did we respond? - impact started at 18:03 UTC on 2 Feb when the periodic remediation workflow began. end: How did we respond? - at 06:05 UTC on 3 Feb backlogs finished, services were back to normal and all impact was declared mitigated. regions: What happened? - multiple regions unnamed; GitHub Actions hit in every region; managed identity failures in East US and West US.
notes: no publication date shown; the unlabeled date 02/02/2026 at the top matches the incident date. Scope coded global because the report says all regions were impacted for GitHub Actions; for the Azure services it says only multiple regions, without names, and the policy propagated broadly across public cloud regions. Only East US and West US are named (managed identity impact). Primary impact was mitigated about 00:30 UTC on 3 Feb in all regions except East US and West US; managed identity impact in those two regions ran 00:08 to 06:05 UTC, partly backlog processing, but no earlier impact-end time is given. region_starts empty: 00:08 UTC is the start of the secondary managed identity impact, and the report does not say East US and West US were unaffected earlier. services_n: 21 distinct services, with Azure Database for PostgreSQL and its Flexible Servers counted once and AKS counted once.

evidence: start: How did we respond? - first customer impact occurred at 08:05 UTC on 22 Dec. end: How did we respond? - at 18:30 UTC, after the rollback, error rates were back to normal and impact was declared mitigated. regions: What happened? - no region is named; a subset of customers of the PIM service was affected.
notes: no publication date shown; the unlabeled date 12/22/2025 at the top matches the incident date. Scope unclear: no region named for the impact (the rollback repair item mentions all regions, but not impact). end_basis impact_ended because the report states error rates had returned to normal. The configuration change deployment started 15 Dec 2025 and reached the heavy-workload ring 19 Dec 2025, before impact. Only Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management is named as impaired.

evidence: start: How did we respond? - impact started at 11:04 EST on 8 Dec. end: How did we respond? - at 14:13 EST all customer impact was declared mitigated. regions: What happened? and What went wrong - every Azure Government region was affected because the authorization policy data is replicated globally.
notes: no publication date shown; the unlabeled date 12/08/2025 at the top matches the incident date. Times are given in EST, not UTC; converted with UTC-5 (standard time on 8 Dec 2025). Scope coded global because the report says all regions of the Azure Government cloud were affected; the scope is limited to that sovereign cloud, Azure public cloud is not stated as affected, and no region is named, so no codes. A similar issue in Azure in China earlier that day is a separate incident. services_n counts the 20 listed services (Azure Policy and Power Platform each once, with their sub-features).
